text: If you are planning a Vietnam tour from India, stop right here. You have clicked on the perfect video. In the next few minutes, I will give you a complete Vietnam tour plan covering North, Central, and South Vietnam. You will learn about the best time to visit, visa process, flights, family, and honeymoon itineraries along with transport and accommodation tips. But here's the big question. What's the ideal number of days to explore Vietnam without missing on its best experiences? Is it 8, 10, or 12 days? Well, before we get into that, let's first understand Vietnam better. Vietnam located in Southeast Asia is divided into three main regions. Hanoi, Halong Bay, and Ninbin with stunning landscapes and cultural heritage forming the northern side of the country. While Daang Hoyan famous for beaches, lantern towns and imperial history is in central Vietnam. Ho Chi Min City, Meong Delta and Fukquok Island known for modern lifestyles, floating markets and island resorts forming the country's southern part. Now that you know the three main regions of Vietnam, the question is which season is best to cover all of them comfortably? The best time to visit Vietnam is during October to April when the weather is pleasant across most regions. Summer May to August can be hot and humid but is good for beach lovers while the monsoon season that is September brings heavy rain in some areas. But what's the smartest way to divide your days across these regions? Whether you are planning for an 8 day, 10day, or 12-day tour to Vietnam, here is an itinerary for each duration. Let's begin with the 12-day tour plan. And then I will customize it for 8 and 10 days. But please remember, the more days you have, the more comfortably you can explore all the parts of this beautiful country. Day one. On the first day of our Vietnam tour, we landed in Hanoi, the famous city in the north. You will easily get direct flights from all major Indian cities to Vietnam. And that made our journey smooth, taking around 5 hours. The e visa process was easy and we cleared immigration quickly. After a short rest at the hotel, we began exploring Hanoi's old quarter in the evening. The narrow streets were full of shops, cafes, and street vendors selling everything from shuvenas to sizzling Vietnamese snacks. We also walked around 1 p.m. Lake, a peaceful spot in the middle of the city. As the sun set, we enjoyed the famous water puppet show, a traditional performance that we all enjoyed. Day two, our second day was reserved for exploring Hanoi's history. We started with the Ho Chi Min Mosolum where we learned about the country's most respected leader. Next, we visited the OnePillar Pagota followed by the Temple of Literature, which was Vietnam's first university built in, 2017. Later in the afternoon, we headed to Trunkwalk Pagoda, the oldest Buddhist temple in Hanoi, standing beautifully by the lake. In the evening, we strolled through the night market, testing local street food and shopping for handmade crops. Day three. On the third day, we went to Ninb, often called Halong Bay on land. We took a small boat through Tamco Cake surrounded by rice fields and limestone mountains. [Music] Then we climbed the Mua Cave viewpoint which gave us a panoramic view. [Music] Day four. On the fourth day, we set out for Halong Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage site around 3 hours from Hanoi. Boarding our cruise ship, we sailed among thousands of limestone islands rising from emerald waters. We explored hidden caves, went kayaking, enjoyed fresh seafood lunch on the deck. The beauty of the bay felt like something out of a painting. It was one of the most memorable days of our trip. Day five. On the fifth morning, we flew to Dhanang, located in central Vietnam. From there, a short drive took us to Hoan, a charming ancient town. We checked into a cozy riverside hotel and then explored the lantern lit streets in the evening. Goan felt magical with colorful lanterns hangering across the streets, tailor shops, and little cafes along the river. We also took a short boat ride where we released paper lanterns into the water making wishes. Day six. The sixth day was dedicated to Bana Hills, a fantasy theme park in the mountains. A thrilling cable car ride took us up offering stunning views. The highlight was the golden bridge held up by two giant stone hands, a mustsee for everyone. We also visited the flower gardens, French village, and fun indoor games at Fantasy Park. By evening, we returned to Hoyan to relax by the river. Day seven. On the seventh day, we flew south to Ho Chi Min City, Vietnam's largest city. Our first stop was the Coochie Tunnels, an underground network used during Vietnam War. Crawling through the narrow tunnels was adventurous, but best suited for adults and older kids. Later we explored Benthan market full of shuveners, handiccrafts and local snacks. Day eight. The eighth day was reserved for the Meong Delta. We drove a couple of hours out of the city and boarded a wooden boat. Floating past coconut plantations, fruit orchards, and small villages gave us a glimpse of rural Vietnam. By evening, we returned to Ho Chi Min City. In the evening, we boarded a Saigon River dinner cruise, enjoying the skyline lit up with skyscrapers and colonial buildings. Day nine. On the ninth day, we flew to Folk Island, Vietnam's tropical paradise. After checking into our beachfront resort, we relaxed at Long Beach, famous for its golden sands and stunning sunset. Day 10. The 10th day was dedicated to exploring the island's attractions. We started with the Fukquok cable car, one of the longest oversea cable cars in the world, which took us to Hon Island for water activities. [Music] In the afternoon, we visited Sao Beach, one of the most beautiful beaches in Vietnam with powdery white sand and turquoise water. Later, we spent the evening at Grand World Fukwalk, a massive entertainment complex with colorful Venice style canels, light shows, shopping, and lively performances. Day 11. On our final day, we went on an island hopping tour by speedboat. We visited smaller islands around Fukquok such as Gangghi Island for snorkeling, Mirat Island for swimming, and coral reefs filled with tropical fish. It was a day full of sea, sun, and adventure. By late afternoon, we returned to our resort. Day 12. On the 12th day, we headed to the airport for our flight back to Ho Chi Min City connecting onward to India. Now you know where to stay in each city depending on your style and budget. But how do you actually move around Vietnam efficiently? Vietnam has convenient domestic flights between Hanoi, Daang and Ho Chi Min City. For local travel, taxis and private cars can be hired for sightseeing. Trains and buses are budget options, but families prefer flights for comfort. Hope you got all the information you need to plan your Vietnam trip.
